from_quote: Each house shall be a judge of the elections, returns and qualifications of its own members— a majority shall constitute a quorum, and be authorized to compel the attendance of absent members, in such manner and under such penalties as the law may provide.
rationale: Cites "Section 5" and reproduces this clause in close but abridged wording, without quotation marks.
to_quote: Each House shall be the Judge of the Elections, Returns and Qualifications of its own Members, and a Majority of each shall constitute a Quorum to do Business

from_quote: Each house shall determine the rules of its proceedings — punish its members for disorderly behaviour — and with the consent of two-thirds, expel a member.
rationale: Reproduces this clause nearly word for word as part of what "Section 5, of the new constitution, says."
to_quote: Each House may determine the Rules of its Proceedings, punish its Members for disorderly Behaviour, and, with the Concurrence of two thirds, expel a Member.

from_quote: Each house shall keep a journal of its proceedings, and from time to time publish the same, &c.
rationale: Reproduces the opening of this clause verbatim as part of what "Section 5, of the new constitution, says."
to_quote: Each House shall keep a Journal of its Proceedings, and from time to time publish the same

from_quote: Sect. 5, further provides, That each house shall keep a journal of its proceedings, and from time to time publish the same, &c.
rationale: Cites "Sect. 5" and reproduces the opening of this clause verbatim.
to_quote: Each House shall keep a Journal of its Proceedings, and from time to time publish the same

from_quote: Sect. 6, provides. That the senators and representatives shall receive a compensation for their services, to be ascertained by law
rationale: Cites "Sect. 6" and reproduces this clause, verbatim at first and then abridged, including the privilege from arrest and the speech or debate provision ("No member shall be called to account for sentiments delivered in either house").
to_quote: The Senators and Representatives shall receive a Compensation for their Services, to be ascertained by Law

from_quote: The 6th section further provides, that no senator or representative shall, during the time he is in office, be elected or appointed to any office under the United States
rationale: Cites "The 6th section" and paraphrases this clause on members holding other offices.
to_quote: no Person holding any Office under the United States, shall be a Member of either House during his Continuance in Office

from_quote: Sect. 7 provides that all bills for raising revenues shall originate in the house of representatives.
rationale: Cites "Sect. 7" and reproduces this clause's first part nearly verbatim ("revenues" for "Revenue").
to_quote: All Bills for raising Revenue shall originate in the House of Representatives

from_quote: The 7th section further provides. That every bill which passes the house of representatives and the senate, before it becomes a law, shall be presented to the president of the United States
rationale: Cites "The 7th section" and paraphrases this clause on presenting bills to the President and repassing them by two-thirds.
to_quote: Every Bill which shall have passed the House of Representatives and the Senate, shall, before it become a Law, be presented to the President of the United States

from_quote: Sect. 8 provides, That Congress shall have power to lay and •collect taxes, duties, imposts, excises, &c. — to pay debts, to provide for the common defence and general welfare of the United States — that all duties, imposts and excises shall be uniform throughout the Union
rationale: Cites "Sect. 8" and reproduces this clause closely, with "the Union" for "the United States" at the end (the stray "•" is OCR damage).
to_quote: The Congress shall have Power To lay and collect Taxes, Duties, Imposts and Excises, to pay the Debts and provide for the common Defence and general Welfare of the United States; but all Duties, Imposts and Excises shall be uniform throughout the United States

from_quote: they shall have power to coin money, and to fix the value thereof, &c.
rationale: Names, as part of what "Sect. 8 provides," the power "to coin money, and to fix the value thereof," which is this clause.
to_quote: To coin Money, regulate the Value thereof

from_quote: Section Qth says, The writ of habeus corpus shall not be suspended, unless in case of rebellion, or the invasion of the publick safety may require it.
rationale: Cites "Section Qth" (OCR "Q" for "9") and reproduces this clause with small differences of wording.
to_quote: The Privilege of the Writ of Habeas Corpus shall not be suspended, unless when in Cases of Rebellion or Invasion the public Safety may require it.

from_quote: The 9th section further provides, that a regular statement and account of the receipts and expenditures of all publick monies, shall be published from time to time.
rationale: Cites "The 9th section" and reproduces the second part of this clause nearly verbatim.
to_quote: a regular Statement and Account of the Receipts and Expenditures of all public Money shall be published from time to time

from_quote: no state shall enter into any treaty, alliance, &c., coin money, emit bills of credit, make any other but gold and silver coin a tender in payment of debts
rationale: Cites "The last section of this article" (Article I, Section 10) and reproduces this clause in abridged form.
to_quote: No State shall enter into any Treaty, Alliance, or Confederation; grant Letters of Marque and Reprisal; coin Money; emit Bills of Credit; make any Thing but gold and silver Coin a Tender in Payment of Debts

from_quote: all laws respecting imposts, duties, and excises, shall be subject to the revision and controul of Congress
rationale: Names, from "The last section of this article," the provision that state laws on imposts and duties "shall be subject to the revision and controul of Congress," the words of this clause.
to_quote: all such Laws shall be subject to the Revision and Controul of the Congress

from_quote: the words of which are, "all powers Herein Granted."
rationale: Quotes in quotation marks the words "all powers Herein Granted" from this clause, which Cassius quoted in full in Cassius.8.3.

from_quote: Section one, of article second, provides that the executive power shall be vested in a president of the United States.
rationale: Cites "Section one, of article second" and reproduces the first sentence of this clause verbatim.
to_quote: The executive Power shall be vested in a President of the United States

from_quote: that Congress shall determine the time for choosing electors, and the day of election shall be the same throughout the Union
rationale: Cites "the same section" (Article II, Section 1) and paraphrases this clause on the time of choosing electors.
to_quote: The Congress may determine the Time of chusing the Electors, and the Day on which they shall give their Votes; which Day shall be the same throughout the United States.
